an5.17:1.1: “Bhikkhus, possessing five qualities, a bhikkhu is practicing for his own welfare but not for the welfare of others.
an5.17:1.3: (1) Here, a bhikkhu is himself accomplished in virtuous behavior but does not encourage others to become accomplished in virtuous behavior;
an5.17:1.4: (2) he is himself accomplished in concentration but does not encourage others to become accomplished in concentration;
an5.17:1.5: (3) he is himself accomplished in wisdom but does not encourage others to become accomplished in wisdom;
an5.17:1.6: (4) he is himself accomplished in liberation but does not encourage others to become accomplished in liberation;
an5.17:1.7: (5) he is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation but does not encourage others to become accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation.
an5.17:1.8: Possessing these five qualities, a bhikkhu is practicing for his own welfare but not for the welfare of others.”
